A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PCD metric and SensorRainFall research. Their text, equations, figures, and tables are readable, including v2's supplementary Sections 7–9. Retained material can be matched across restructuring and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original detector evaluations, estimated variance change points, and threshold-sensitivity results on SensorRainFall in Tables 2–3 and Figures 4–6.

after.justification: v2 reports expanded detection and segmentation experiments in Tables 1 and 3–10, plus original synthetic change-point simulations in Section 5.3.

M1.justification: Both versions use IoU × confidence, spline mean estimation, recursive variance-change testing, Gaussian exceedance probabilities, and the same maximum-distance rule. Renaming mPCD to aPCD preserves the threshold-aggregation construction; segmentation experiments do not introduce a new PCD procedure.

E1.justification: Coverage expands from vehicle detection under clear and rainy daylight to vehicle and pedestrian detection and instance segmentation across four conditions, adding rainy night with and without streetlights. These are substantive changes in targets, task requirements, and illumination conditions.

E2.justification: The five original object detectors remain. v2 additionally evaluates Mask R-CNN, ConvNeXt-V2, SOLOv2, Mask2Former, and RTMDet in the segmentation comparisons, as documented in Tables 9–10.

E3.justification: v2 adds AR and F150 evaluation and controlled simulation protocols varying sample sizes, change-point counts, and variance contrasts. Supplement Section 9 also reports YOLOX depth/width factors of 1.33/1.25 versus v1's 0.33/0.5, although v2's main text retains the old factors. This establishes conflicting reported settings, not verified rerunning.

E4.justification: New Section 5.3 tests change-point detection sensitivity to sample size and effect size. Figures 5–6 add model-pair case studies explaining metric disagreements, and Figure 7 extends threshold-sensitivity analysis to nighttime conditions. These substantially expand the analytical support beyond v1's daylight analyses.

E5.justification: Section 5.3 newly specifies 1,000 replications per sample-size/change-point-count combination, with means and standard deviations in Figure 8. This uncertainty reporting is confined to the simulation; benchmark tables still lack reported repeated-run uncertainty, and the existing alpha = 0.05 change-point criterion remains.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive nighttime, pedestrian, segmentation, and simulation results. Retained clear-daylight scores also change: Deformable DETR's aggregate PCD is 106.275 versus 104.855 m, and AP50 is 0.953 versus 0.947 in v1 Table 3 and v2 Table 7. Original rainy-daylight scores and change-point locations are retained. The PDFs do not explain all numerical revisions.

T1.justification: The formal PCD definition, Gaussian assumptions, spline objective, and variance-change test remain mathematically equivalent. Section 5.3 restates the existing rejection rule in equivalent probability form and adds empirical simulations, rather than new theory or proofs.

C1.justification: PCD and the controlled SensorRainFall benchmark remain the central contributions. The abstract, introduction, and conclusion broaden the explicitly claimed dataset and validation scope to illumination variation and segmentation, while retaining the central claim of distance-dependent reliability beyond static metrics.

C2.justification: v2 adds safety-envelope interpretations, application-specific threshold guidance, and variance/failure-tail explanations for disagreements with conventional metrics. It also changes the threshold interpretation: v1 Section 5.2.3 describes abrupt rainy-daylight behavior, whereas v2 Section 5.2 describes both daylight surfaces as smooth and emphasizes nighttime instability.

D1.justification: Supplement Sections 7 and 9 substantially expand documentation of sensor synchronization, DGPS distances, lighting, target placement, pedestrian coverings, checkpoints, preprocessing, optimization, and model configurations. Most are newly disclosed details rather than demonstrated changes to existing experiments. The code/data links and computing environment remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially broadens the evaluation-metric context by discussing LRP/oLRP, PDQ, JIoU, and GIoU, extending positioning beyond conventional and temporal metrics to localization and uncertainty-aware evaluation. Additional segmentation and statistical references support the expanded scope; these citations alone are not experimental comparisons.

P1.justification: The method section is reordered to present PCD computation first, and experiments are reorganized around representative comparisons, insights, and estimator validation. Full results and configurations move into supplementary sections. The abstract and explanatory passages are extensively rewritten, with mPCD renamed aPCD throughout.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a two-column layout, redraws the conceptual PCD figure, expands dataset and threshold panels, and adds model-comparison, simulation, and annotation figures. Dataset and benchmark tables are relocated, restructured, and expanded in the supplement, with a new representative-results table in the main text.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially addresses v1's narrow vehicle-only daylight validation and absence of empirical testing of the change-point estimator through broader experiments and replicated simulations. Expanded related work and implementation documentation further strengthen the paper. Unreconciled rainfall descriptions (64 versus 20/40 mm/h), conflicting YOLOX configurations, and unexplained score revisions weaken reproducibility, but the new evidence substantially improves support for the central evaluation framework.
